sections.description:
THE ANTI-CORRUPTION LAWS (APPLICATION TO TRIBAL AREAS) REGULATION, 1966
THE ANTI-CORRUPTION LAWS (APPLICATION TO TRIBAL AREAS) REGULATION, 1966
(West Pakistan
Regulation I of 1966)
A Regulation to apply certain
anti-corruption laws to the Tribal Areas of the Peshawar and Quetta Division. (Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, 22nd March, 1966).
S.R. 36(R)/66.--The following Regulation made by the President of
Pakistan on the 8th March, 1966 is hereby published for general information.
Whereas it is expedient to apply
certain anti-corruption laws to the Tribal Areas of the Peshawar and Quetta Divisions.
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (2) of Article 223 of Constitution, the
President is pleased to make the following Regulations.
1. Short title and commencement.--(1) This Regulation may be called
the Anti-Corruption Laws (Application to Tribal Areas) Regulation 1966.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.
2. Application of certain laws to certain Tribal Areas.--(1) The
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, (II of 1947), the Pakistan Special Police Establishment
Ordinance, 1948 (VIII of 1948), and the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1958 (XL of 1958), shall apply to the Tribal Areas of the Peshawar Division as
they apply to other parts of West Pakistan.
(2) The Pakistan Criminal Law
Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958), shall apply to the Tribal Areas of Quetta
Division as it applies other parts of West Pakistan.
